newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Suzuki may up Hungary output 10,000 units.
newsitem.headline: Suzuki may up Hungary output 10,000 units.

text.p: Japanese automaker Suzuki Motor Corp said on Friday it might increase its car production in Hungary another 10,000 units a year to 60,000 units annually without specifying when it might happen.
Hungarian news agency MTI reported on Thursday that Suzuki said output at its Hungarian plant, Magyar Suzuki Rt, could rise 10,000 each year in coming years without offering further details.
But Tamas Tihanyi, Magyar Suzuki's public relations manager, told Reuters on Friday the company had no plans to increase its output 10,000 units annually.
"Suzuki cars from Hungary are popular in Europe as well as Hungary, and we might increase our output to 60,000 units a year," Tihanyi said.
But 60,000 units is the maximum capacity at Magyar Suzuki, and the company had no plans to increase its investment to add capacity, Tihany said.
Magyar Suzuki, which has built and sold Suzuki Swift hatchbacks and sedans since 1992, built roughly 52,000 cars in 1996, and it plans to make 54,000 units in 1997.
